stem: Who is **technical documentation** mainly written for?

options.content: Programmers and technicians who maintain the system
options.rationale: Correct: it explains how the system was built.

options.content: Customers who buy goods from the business
options.rationale: Customers do not use system documentation.

options.content: Clerks who enter data into the system each day
options.rationale: Clerks need the user documentation.

options.content: Managers who approve the project's budget
options.rationale: They need the feasibility report.

explanation: Technical documentation is for the people who maintain, correct and improve the system.

stem: Which item would be found in **user** documentation?

options.content: Step-by-step instructions for printing a report
options.rationale: Correct: users need to know how to carry out tasks.

options.content: A listing of the program code with comments
options.rationale: Code belongs in technical documentation.

options.content: The data dictionary of every table
options.rationale: Data structures belong in technical documentation.

options.content: The algorithms written in pseudocode
options.rationale: Algorithms belong in technical documentation.

explanation: User documentation explains how to use the system to do tasks.

stem: Why is technical documentation especially important when the original programmer leaves the company?

options.content: Users can learn how to log in to the system
options.rationale: That is in user documentation.

options.content: It stops the system from ever needing changes
options.rationale: All systems need maintenance.

options.content: It replaces the need to test the system
options.rationale: Testing is still needed.

options.content: A new programmer can understand the system and maintain it
options.rationale: Correct: the knowledge is kept in writing.

explanation: Without technical documentation, a new programmer would struggle to fix or change the system.

stem: A clerk sees the message *Database locked by another user*. Which section of the user guide should she read?

options.content: Glossary of terms
options.rationale: A glossary explains words, not errors.

options.content: Troubleshooting (error messages)
options.rationale: Correct: it explains error messages and what to do.

options.content: Hardware requirements
options.rationale: This lists equipment needed.

options.content: Version history
options.rationale: This belongs in technical documentation.

explanation: The troubleshooting section lists error messages with their causes and solutions.

stem: Which is the **main** reason for training users before a new system goes live?

options.content: So the programmers can stop writing documentation
options.rationale: Documentation is still needed.

options.content: So the hardware lasts longer
options.rationale: Training does not affect hardware life.

options.content: So the system needs no backups
options.rationale: Backups are still needed.

options.content: So they use it correctly and make fewer errors
options.rationale: Correct: trained users enter data accurately and efficiently.

explanation: Training reduces errors, increases efficiency and helps users accept the new system.
hints: What happens if staff do not know how to use a system?

stem: A bank must train 300 tellers in branches across Zimbabwe on a new feature. Which training method is **most** practical?

options.content: One classroom course in Harare for all 300 tellers
options.rationale: Bringing 300 staff to one place is costly and closes branches.

options.content: Online video tutorials and e-learning
options.rationale: Correct: staff in every branch can learn at their own pace without travel.

options.content: The programmer visits each teller in turn
options.rationale: This would take far too long.

options.content: Giving each teller the program listing
options.rationale: Tellers do not need the code.

explanation: E-learning suits large numbers of staff spread over many places.
hints: Who is spread out, and who needs to learn at their own pace?

stem: A shop gives its staff only the user manual instead of a training course. What is the **most likely** problem?

options.content: The manual will cost more than the course
options.rationale: A manual is usually much cheaper.

options.content: The staff will be away from work for several days
options.rationale: This is a disadvantage of a course, not a manual.

options.content: Some staff will not read it and will make mistakes
options.rationale: Correct: self-study relies on staff reading the manual.

options.content: The manual will contain program listings
options.rationale: A user manual should not contain code.

explanation: Manuals are cheap and always available, but some users never read them and have no one to ask.

stem: User documentation should be written in plain, non-technical language.
explanation: True. Users are not programmers, so instructions must be simple, clear and illustrated.

stem: All documentation is written only after the system has been fully installed.
explanation: False. Documentation is built up throughout the project (requirements, designs, test results) and completed at implementation.

stem: Classify each item as user or technical documentation.

left.content: How to log in and change your password

explanation: Log-in instructions and FAQs are for users; code and test results are for programmers.

stem: Match each training method to an advantage.

right.content: Staff learn at their own pace and time
Help is always available inside the program
Skills are learnt in the real work situation

explanation: Course: immediate answers. On-the-job: real situation. E-learning: own pace. Help screens: always there.
hints: Think about cost, pace and where it happens.

payload.template: The section of a user guide that explains unfamiliar words is the {{blank:a}}. The part of the technical documentation that records what has changed in each release is the version {{blank:b}}.

hints: One lists meanings of words; one lists past changes.

stem: Give the other name for the printed user documentation that explains how to operate a system (two words).
explanation: User documentation is often called the user guide or user manual.

stem: State **four** items that should be included in technical documentation.

points.description: Program listings with comments / algorithms (pseudocode, flowcharts)
File structures / data dictionary / database design
Test plan and results / hardware and software requirements / known bugs / version history

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The commented program code, the data dictionary showing each table and field, the system flowchart, and the test plan with its test data and results.

explanation: Technical documentation records how the system was designed, built and tested.
hints: What does a programmer need to change the system?

stem: Explain why different users of a new hospital system need different training, and why training is important for the hospital.

points.description: Different users do different tasks (e.g. receptionists book, doctors record diagnoses, technicians do backups)
So each group is trained in the features they use / access levels differ
Importance: fewer data entry errors (e.g. wrong patient records)
Importance: efficient use / user acceptance / security awareness

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Receptionists only book appointments, while doctors record diagnoses and technicians manage backups, so each group needs training in the features it uses. Training means fewer mistakes in patients' records, staff work faster, and they accept the new system instead of resisting it.

explanation: Training should match each user's job, and it reduces errors and resistance.
hints: Give a consequence for each reason.

stem: Chipo's Supermarket (fictional) in Bulawayo is installing a new point-of-sale system in its four branches. It employs 30 cashiers and one IT technician.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which document does the IT technician need to change the discount rules in the code?

options.content: User documentation
options.rationale: It explains how to use the system.

options.content: The feasibility report
options.rationale: This is an early project document.

options.content: Technical documentation
options.rationale: Correct: it explains the code and data structures.

options.content: The questionnaire results
options.rationale: These are fact-finding results.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Classify each item for the supermarket's documentation.

left.content: How to void an item on a sale
What to do if the scanner stops working

parts.explanation: Voiding a sale and scanner troubleshooting: user. Table structure: technical.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Recommend a training method for the 30 cashiers and justify it.

points.description: A suitable method (e.g. hands-on instructor-led session / on-the-job training at the till)
Justification linked to the scenario (practice on real tills / questions answered / little time away from work)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: On-the-job training at the tills, given by a trained supervisor in each branch, because cashiers learn on the real equipment and the shops stay open.

hints: Users need tasks; programmers need structure and code.

stem: A Gweru software company is writing user documentation for a farm records app used by farmers with little computer experience.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: The user guide should include the data dictionary of the app's database.
parts.explanation: False: farmers do not need data structures; that is technical documentation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Describe **four** features that would make the user documentation suitable for these farmers.

points.description: Plain, non-technical language / glossary for any terms
Step-by-step instructions with screenshots or pictures
Short videos or built-in help screens / available offline
Troubleshooting / FAQs / index and contact details for support

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It should use plain language with a glossary, give step-by-step instructions with screenshots, include short videos that work offline, and have a troubleshooting section with a phone number for support.
